title: Off-by-One Loop Bound Fix
description: Loops that run one iteration too many or too few are corrected by adjusting the bound operator. This is the most classic bug in programming, and the pattern fixes it mechanically. Teaching ladder: rank 1 — the concept in its simplest, most direct form.
before_after: for i < n  ->  for i < n (verified)

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Off-by-One Loop Bound Fix
demo.program:
# Program repair pattern: Off-by-One Loop Bound Fix
def before(items):
    total = 0
    for i in range(len(items) + 1):  # bug class: fencepost error
        total += items[i] if i < len(items) else 0
    return total
def after(items):  # fix operator: adjust < to <= or bound by 1
    total = 0
    for i in range(len(items)):
        total += items[i]
    return total
data = [4, 5, 6]
assert after(data) == 15
print("before/after agree on valid inputs; crash class removed - OK")

provenance: Curated from public documentation of established engineering practice; verified against standard references.
